And I say also unto thee, That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.*

**1 Corinthians 3:9-11**
*For we are labourers together with God: ye are God's husbandry, ye are God's building. According to the grace of God which is given unto me, as a wise masterbuilder, I have laid the foundation, and another buildeth thereon. But let every man take heed how he buildeth thereupon. For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ.*

**Isaiah 2:2-4**
*And it shall come to pass in the last days, that the mountain of the LORD's house shall be established in the top of the mountains, and shall be exalted above the hills; and all nations shall flow unto it.* *And many people shall go and say, Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem. And he shall judge among the nations, and shall rebuke many people: and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks: nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.*

teachings.title: A healthy church keeps its shibboleths
teachings.theme: Christ the foundation of the church
teachings.summary: He welcomes the charge that fundamentalists keep shibboleths like separation and the KJB, the main one being the gospel of grace by which false teachers are known.
teachings.text:
After Jephthah's tragic victory in **Judges 11**, he finds himself in a similar situation as Gideon had a century earlier, back in **Judges 8**;

*And the men of Ephraim said unto him, Why hast thou served us thus, that thou calledst us not, when thou wentest to fight with the Midianites? And they did chide with him sharply.*

Here in **Judges 12**, rather than deescalate the conflict with the men of Ephraim with kind words as Gideon had, Jephthah chooses conflict and he and his men smite the men of Ephraim, driving them back across the Jordan.

It is here we get the term 'Shibboleth,' a word that the Ephraimites struggled to pronounce as the Gileadites did. By asking the fleeing men to say it, knowing it would betray them as of Ephraim, Gilead put them to the sword.

This shows that even just a few hundred years since Moses and the settling of the land by Israel, that distinct dialects and regional accents had occurred. The tribes of Israel were themselves nations. And subgroups like Gilead, which was the name of part of the land settled by Gad, on the east bank of the Jordan, had grown to be its own thing. God sets boundaries and habitations, dividing nations by blood and language, shifting over time as He judges them.

We often see the term 'Shibboleth' used today as a derogatory way of describing a longstanding belief that a group of people may share that separates them from others. A way of gatekeeping looked down upon by those with modernist views, seeking to infiltrate and influence the older group.

There have been those who have accused fundamentalists of maintaining Shibboleths, from matters of separation to the sole use of the KJB, and even to the nature of the gospel...All have been attacked as 'archaic' means of resisting change in the modern era, and to that we should say "Amen!"

Scripture tells us repeatedly of how we can recognize false teachers and warns of those creeping in privily, unawares, to spy out our liberty and to lead believers astray. The main shibboleth being the gospel of grace and reconciliation through faith in Christ. If someone brings a false gospel, we know they are not of God but accursed.

**Galatians 1:8-9**
*But though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed. As we said before, so say I now again, If any man preach any other gospel unto you than that ye have received, let him be accursed.*

A healthy church maintains the landmark shibboleths of the faith.

teachings.title: Upon this rock: Christ, not Peter
teachings.theme: Christ the foundation of the church
teachings.summary: The rock the church is built on is the truth that Jesus is the Christ, not Peter as Rome claims, and taking up the cross was a literal call for the apostles.
teachings.text:
Later on, Jesus brings up the rumors of Him going around to the Twelve, who had been journeying throughout the land, now returned. He asks who do the people say I am? They say, like Herod, people wonder if He is John, or a prophet returned. But when He asks them who they think He is, *Peter answering said, The Christ of God.*

Here in Luke, the narrative moves to Jesus' admonishment to keep that quiet that His fate be allowed to play out. In **John 16**, in scripture that is taken out of context by Roman Catholics to justify their false church, Jesus replies to Peter's profession of faith that He is the Christ by saying that truth is the rock upon which His church is built. Catholic tradition twists this to make Peter that rock, and claim their earthly church was founded that day on a man, rather than Jesus and His Heavenly assembly of those who know He is Christ and believe.

It is worth mentioning only in that if their version were true, it is odd that it's overlooked everywhere else in the Gospels, and in context, not even present in John.

But affirming He is the Christ, as eleven of the Twelve believe, He again prepares them, that He must suffer and die, and rise again. Betrayed and rejected. And warns of any follow Him, to be prepared to take up their own cross daily, and follow Him unto death. That if they deny Him to save their own lives, they will lose it, but those willing to be faithful unto death will live.

We draw a spiritual doctrine from this verse, inspiration to get up every day willing to sacrifice, follow His commandments, read the Bible, pray, etc. Taking up our cross. But here, Jesus means it literally, as well. They are going to face death for His sake. They will be tempted to deny Him. To be ashamed of the word. His Gospel. And Jesus wants them to understand if they don't truly have faith in Him they will falter, seek to save themselves and in doing so, lose out on the Kingdom, He will say He never knew them when He comes into His glory. "Lord, Lord..." and all.

Again, we take from this spiritual application, and pastors will preach on how this is a lesson for us in improving our Christian walk, and it indubitably is. It is something that has comforted and edified me, and still does. It's something I try to remind myself of, especially those days you wake up not really feeling it. Cares of the world, infirmities of the flesh. Inspired by Jesus calling us to take up our cross and follow Him.

But for us it's not sleeping in, or turning to the word instead of sin or remembering to pray. For His disciples, it was literal.

teachings.title: The Lukewarm Church of Laodicea
teachings.theme: Christ the foundation of the church
teachings.summary: Christ rebukes comfortable lukewarm churches out of love, and the church ages teaching that we live in a Laodicean age is false and breeds complacency.
teachings.text:
*And unto the angel of the church of the Laodiceans write; These things saith the Amen, the faithful and true witness, the beginning of the creation of God;*

The Amen! Jesus is the Amen, the 'let it be' of God. Verily. True. Through whom all things were created and through whom all things are fulfilled. Unto the Laodiceans.

*I know thy works, that thou art neither cold nor hot: I would thou wert cold or hot. So then because thou art lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will spue thee out of my mouth.*

They are neither hot nor cold. They aren't doing much of anything for the Lord. A church that's lukewarm, does the bare minimum without any enthusiasm. Who haven't gone the way of dying off, apostasy, just grown cold to the truth of the word and aren't really living it. Comfortable. But this offense the Lord more than if they had just grown cold. Mailing it in is more offensive to God, and that's understandable. Many churches are this way. That is why the false doctrine of these churches representing ages claim we are living in the "Laodicean age." It's an easy comparison that allows a pastor to "rah rah" some life out of their members, but it being a false doctrine can lock congregations into complacency. "Sure the church isn't doing much, but it is the age we love in. Oh well."

Meanwhile there are churches who are on fire for the Lord. There's always a remnant. 7000 who haven't bent the knee to Baal. And a dead or dying church can always be revived, this is the point of these messages from Christ Jesus Himself, to encourage and edify. Warn and chastise.

But complacency is often found in comfort.

*Because thou sayest, I am rich, and increased with goods, and have need of nothing; and knowest not that thou art wretched, and miserable, and poor, and blind, and naked: I counsel thee to buy of me gold tried in the fire, that thou mayest be rich; and white raiment, that thou mayest be clothed, and that the shame of thy nakedness do not appear; and anoint thine eyes with eyesalve, that thou mayest see.*

Jesus is attacking that comfort. Saying they have physical wealth and are doing well, as many congregations are today, but they need to recognize they are poor; wretched and miserable. Blind to the word and naked in their sin.

He says to buy Him gold tried in the fire, ala **1 Corinthians 3.** Spiritual wealth, that comes from good works; spreading the Gospel, winning souls, caring for the least of us. Having the white raiment that comes from believing unto salvation and that covers our nakedness before God. Anointing their eyes with the word, being doers not just hearers, that they may see.

And Jesus' harsh criticism is leveled against these churches out of love.

*As many as I love, I rebuke and chasten: be zealous therefore, and repent. Behold, I stand at the door, and knock: if any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in to him, and will sup with him, and he with me*.

Whom God loves, He chasteneth. Scourging every son. But the promise of His fellowship is such that any who open themself up towards Him, He shall come in unto.

And His final message to the saved;

*To him that overcometh will I grant to sit with me in my throne, even as I also overcame, and am set down with my Father in his throne. He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches.*

Again, the promise to rule and reign with Him. Just as God has established Jesus Christ's throne, so too are we made heirs to the Kingdom, serving in the house of the Lord. Amen.

teachings.title: Upon this rock: the confession of Christ
teachings.theme: Christ the foundation of the church
teachings.summary: The rock Christ builds His church on is the truth Peter confessed, that Jesus is the Christ the Son of God, not Peter himself, and believers are lively stones built on it.
teachings.text:
Next we see they've moved on, and having come to Philippi, Jesus is again teaching His Apostles, and begins asking "*Whom do men say that I the Son of man am?*"

The apostles say that the people say *He is John the Baptist: some, Elias; and others, Jeremias, or one of the prophets.* It is interesting that the popular consensus regarding Jesus was that he was first and foremost a hard preaching prophet. John the baptist, Elijah, and especially Jeremiah were known for their fire breathing preaching, condemning sin and wickedness of those around them.

Then Jesus asks, "*But whom say ye that I am*?" And Simon Peter, (*Thou art Simon the son of Jona: thou shalt be called Cephas, which is by interpretation, A stone*), answers, saying "*Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God."*

To which Jesus responds; "*Blessed art thou, Simon Barjona: for flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father which is in heaven. And I say also unto thee, That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it. And I will give unto thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt bind on earth shall be bound in heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.*"

Taken in context, we see that Jesus in confirming Peter's profession of faith, that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, that this truth revealed to Peter by God, and to all of us through His word and received by faith, is the rock upon which Jesus is building his church. His congregation of believers.

We see that Jesus originally calling him cephas or Peter, which translated means a stone, a chip of rock, is here paid off. A long setup punchline, used by Jesus to make a point regarding the gospel being **The Rock**, that the truth of Jesus being the long-awaited Christ is the cornerstone upon which the church is built. And we who believe, as Peter says in his Epistles, are as lively stones like him, making up the edification, the building up of the church, the congregation of which comes together on the day of the Lord.

We know that Jesus, upon his resurrection, had with him the keys to Hell and death. That rock, the truth of the Gospel, this spiritual bread, grants eternal life to those who believe. That the gospel itself is the key. That the truth of it is the rock.

And again these  things that are spiritually discerned, and twisted into perverse doctrines.

In the Catholic heresy, Peter becomes the rock, the church, an earthly institution built by men, the bread literal, and so literally flesh. The leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees added to the word, just as Christ warned.

teachings.title: What makes a true church
teachings.theme: Christ the foundation of the church
teachings.summary: A church is measured by the word preached, sound doctrine, a qualified pastor and soul-winning fruit, not by PayPal or obeying state rules, which Romans 13 says to follow unless they contradict God.
teachings.text:
Any church that uses PayPal for donations isn't a real church.
Or that has occupancy license and obeys fire codes, ADA regs, or any other state regulation.
Or that encourages political action and particular partisan participation in secular elections.

/sarcasm

The word that's preached, not compromising that word, and the fruit of soul winning is the measure of a church and pastor. How they obey primary and secondary biblical doctrine, the pastor being qualified and producing good fruit of saved Christians, is what is important.

How they arrange their finances *could* be a secondary bit of evidence at it being false if other things - unqualified pastor, wrong on primary doctrine, adding to biblical salvation by faith alone in grace alone, mixed assembly, making merchandise of God's house, or His flock, etc - is found, but it certainly is not qualifying or disqualifying on its own.

**Romans 13:1-7**
*Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God.*

*2 Whosoever therefore resisteth the power, resisteth the ordinance of God: and they that resist shall receive to themselves damnation.*

*3 For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to the evil. Wilt thou then not be afraid of the power? do that which is good, and thou shalt have praise of the same:*

*4 For he is the minister of God to thee for good. But if thou do that which is evil, be afraid; for he beareth not the sword in vain: for he is the minister of God, a revenger to execute wrath upon him that doeth evil.*

*5 Wherefore ye must needs be subject, not only for wrath, but also for conscience sake.*

*6 For for this cause pay ye tribute also: for they are God's ministers, attending continually upon this very thing.*

*7 Render therefore to all their dues: tribute to whom tribute is due; custom to whom custom; fear to whom fear; honour to whom honour.*

If the state has rules on how tribute and custom are collected, then follow them to the edification of the Church and obedience to God's ordained powers that be.

If those rules contradict the higher power, especially the highest, God, then we defer to that higher power. Simple as.

teachings.title: Romans 16: fellow labourers in the churches
teachings.theme: Christ the foundation of the church
teachings.summary: Paul's greetings show saved women and men alike labour for the gospel, in local independent churches, plural, while marking those who bring false doctrines.
teachings.text:
Last chapter in the letter to the church at Rome from Paul. It's basically a post script, but there's doctrine in all scripture and definitely here as well.

Note that Paul first praises a woman, Phebe, commending her for her great work laboring for God, spreading the Gospel and being a strength to others in the faith. She is one of many women God immortalized in scripture for their labors.

Many assume because Paul reiterates God's command that women remain silent in church, and not be pastors (a position many men couldn't qualify for either), that Paul was a misogynist or something. But a saved woman is called to give the gospel and save souls and use their gifts to the edification of the church, just as a man is. That there are roles defined for us by God doesn't make us greater or lesser in His service. *There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus.*

Both men and women lose sight of this in current year, and resentments and divisions surrounding this keep us from fulfilling the labors God has for us.

Paul goes on to salute and praise men and women of the faith who are his fellow laborors. Helpers. Being about the business of the Father. Winning souls and edifying the saints. We should strive to be so worthy as to be known in Heaven for the work we do for the Lord. That the *churches* of Christ salute us.

Yes, churches is plural. That's the NT Christian perspective on a church. Local, independent, Jesus-led, pastor-run, gospel-based. A fellowship of like-minded churches. Not a universal church on earth.

We are to avoid people coming in with false Gospels, extra-biblical doctrines and traditions. Verse 18 is a condensed version of the warnings given by Paul elsewhere, Peter and Jude against letting these types creep in unawares to make merchandise of the believers, and feed their bellies in the communal suppers. Taking advantage of the hospitality, and deceiving even believers with false teachings.

We are to be wise about what's good, simple or that is uninformed about the particulars of evil. Wisdom of good gives enough to discern what's evil without dwelling in it.

Paul finishes with praise of God, and in it he dispels the false doctrine of gnostic revelation regarding salvation. That while the OT saints believed in faith a mystery, we now know it is Jesus who is the Christ.

teachings.title: The Lord's supper is a memorial, not a sacrament
teachings.summary: The Lord's supper continues the Passover as a yearly memorial for saved church members with unleavened bread and unfermented juice, not a sacrament, not wine and not literal flesh as Rome teaches.
teachings.text:
Now, understanding that an ordinance in the Bible is a memorial ritual, given by God to picture the thing which we are to remember for future generations, we see the Lord's supper is a continuation of Passover, which pictured Jesus, the Christ to come and the deliverance by God's promise, given in the blood of the lamb, the unleavened bread represented the haste of their salvation from sin, and literally their being cast out of Egypt following the angel of death coming for all the first born in the land.

Jesus is that lamb, who takes away the sins of the world. The bread now, represents His body. The cup poured out, His blood.

It is the same feast, the same observation. It is a memorial and a picture of Christ.

And like passover, a yearly observation, and an ordinance done only among the people. The saved. Those with the circumcision of the heart, and among the congregation. The assembly of believers. What we call today the church. A church is a local assembly, and we see in Leviticus and in Paul's letter to the Corinthians, that both ordinances, passover and the Lord's supper, were not to be done by the unworthy, the unsaved. Paul even says that God has made those who have partaken of it who aren't saved, who didn't do it in memory of Jesus, but for unworthy reasons, that they've been made weak, and sick, and some have been killed for profaning the ordinance.

And so the Lord's supper is a yearly observance, done within the congregation of believers, using the breaking of unleavened bread and the pouring out of the unfermented juice of the vine, done in memory of Jesus.

What it is not: It is not a means of obtaining grace or salvation. It is not a "sacrament," there are not ritual requirements for salvation given in the New Testament.

It is not done with wine. The idea that the yeast of fermentation would be present when all leaven is to be cast out, is absurd. Alcohol is used as a representation of sin throughout the Bible, as is the yeast in bread. Jesus did not bless alcohol and then say it represents His blood. It's profanity bordering on blasphemy to make that claim.

It is not literal. It is generally accepted by most denominations claiming to be of Christ that the ordinances of the Old Testament were symbolic of Christ and salvation, redemption and the resurrection. No one makes the claim that the lamb offered in passover prior to the crucifixion actually became Jesus. That the blood of the lamb offered upon the doorposts transfigured into His. We all recognize ordinances are symbolic, as God says, done as a memorial.

Jesus, who as God gave us this ordinance as a new memorial, says "do this in memory of me."

The blasphemous and foolish literalist view that the bread and alcohol served by these vipers magically transforms into flesh and blood (literally by "hocus pocus" said by a so called priest) is an abomination. Christianity is not a cannibal cult.

There are some protestant sects of Catholicism that don't go that far, but still make out that it is a sacrament, not an ordinance as the Bible calls it, and that while they reject the cannibal aspect, claim that their communion brings "the real presence of Jesus" to them.

Jesus told us that wherever two or three gather in His name, He is there. Those of us saved have the Holy Spirit within us and are in constant connection to God the Father through Christ His Son. The Lord is ever-present in all things, at all times. There is nothing that can hide Him or separate Him from those who believe.

It is foolishness, and making an idol of what should be a memorial. It cheapens it at best. It becomes rote. Done weekly. Done of habit. Whereas ordinances in scripture are special. Holy. Separate. Something done solemnly and with purpose.

Not every right-believing church does it exactly the same. Some do it monthly. Some every 3 months. Many do it during the Holy Week, during their Wednesday night service. Some encourage their congregation to do it in their home, with their family.

teachings.title: The people justified God, being baptized
teachings.summary: Those who were baptized justified God, vindicating His word by an outward sign of faith, while the Pharisees showed their unbelief by refusing; baptism itself does not save.
teachings.text:
And when the messengers of John departed, Jesus begins to preach to the crowds about John the Baptist. Praising him, but reminding them that to be saved, in Heaven is an even greater thing than even being the greatest prophet among men that ever lived.

I get the sense that what Jesus is doing is shoring up John's reputation least any think his doubt was an indictment of the Gospel he had preached. And the crowd responds. The Bible says:

*And all the people that heard him, and the publicans, justified God, being baptized with the baptism of John.*

Now note the word choice here. Most times when we read "justified" we think of being absolved, the remission of sin and absolution from guilt and punishment by grace through faith in Christ.

But note here Luke says the people who heard Jesus, including the sinners like the publicans (who Luke uses often to contrast with the Pharisees, both men of power, secular and sinful vs who are supposed to be holy and righteous), but he writes these people who heard Jesus preach and His praise of John and his ministry JUSTIFIED GOD, being baptized in the baptism of John.

I think this is a key point we shouldn't miss.

Clearly God is not being absolved of sin here. Justified is also used in a legal sense, meaning vindication. That the evidence is sufficient to prove the argument being made. To show that they believed the report, accepted the witness, agreed with the argument, they were baptized, justifying God.

*But the Pharisees and lawyers rejected the counsel of God against themselves, being not baptized of him.*

You see how the act of baptism by believers justifies God, while the rejection of His counsel, not believing Him, not having that faith, is evidenced by their not being baptized.

How faith is made perfect, complete, by an action that is an outward sign to man of the heart of the person, just as the refusal to act shows the abundance of the heart of those who didn't believe.

Baptism itself doesn't save. It is a manifestation of the faith, the substance of things not seen, that can be seen of men. And by not justifying God, the Pharisees show they do not believe.

teachings.title: Baptism and the Lord's supper are pictures
teachings.summary: Baptism and the Lord's supper are the two New Testament ordinances, pictures of Christ that hold no saving power, and turning them or the sabbath into works for salvation is damnable heresy.
teachings.text:
Finishing this section, and the understanding of ordinances and their proper place in our faith, it is important to note that while the ordinances of the Old Testament were done away with in Christ, there are two new ordinances made to which we should adhere. Baptism and the common blessing and eating of bread and drink, communion, what we call the Lord's supper.

Just as the ordinances of the OT held no actual power to forgive sin or earn grace, but were a picture of the Christ to come, so too the ordinances we are told to keep are an image of Christ, a long shadow cast that we remember Him, and the faith we share as saved believers.

In baptism, the believer is immersed in water, dead, buried and risen in the manner reminiscent of Jesus. Going down into death symbolically, and rising up out of the water, born again.

The Lord's supper, likewise, where we are asked by Jesus to remember what He has done for us, the breaking of His body and the spilling of His blood that we may be saved. To recall this when we gather together in an assembly of believers to eat. Not just blessing the food in His name, but seeing the picture of His sacrifice in the breaking of bread and sharing of the wine (juice, not booze). "Do this in remembrance of Me."

This is the purpose of these ordinances, just as the numerous ordinances of the old covenant were.

But, like the Jews at the time of Jesus, the ordinance of the flesh representing the spiritual, become an idol unto themselves, and mistakenly transformed into a work of righteousness. A means of salvation. A means of obtaining grace, (which is an oxymoron).

Some heretical and judaized churches even place keeping of the sabbath as an ordinance, and a work required for salvation, despite the clear teaching that this was a picture, and done away with in the new covenant.

And just like the Pharisees, many have replaced ordinances made for man with requiring the man be made for the ordinance.

And just as the Pharisees' approach led to hypocrisy and their inability to produce fruit, men ripe for repentance, create with their false gospel proselytes twofold more the child of hell than themselves.

Damnable heresy.

teachings.title: John the Baptist and believer's baptism
teachings.summary: John baptized believers by immersion as the answer of a good conscience, not to wash away sin, and his hard preaching told the Pharisees that descent from Abraham would not save them.
teachings.text:
The prophet who comes before Christ. The voice crying out in the wilderness. Telling all men to turn towards God, that the Messiah is coming. John the Baptist.

Jesus cousin, raised by his righteous parents, bringing people to salvation and baptising believers, by immersion, in much water.

Baptism not being the putting away of sin, but the answer of a good conscience by those who have called upon the name of the Lord for forgiveness of sin and everlasting life. The same unbroken line of faith from John to modern, NT Christians. (Note it's not John the Catholic or John the Lutheran)

He eschews comfort. Eats ze bugs. And rips face with hard preaching. Matthew 3 captures a moment of John's style of fire-breathing, hellfire and damnation preaching, in this case against the Pharisees and Sadducees. The religious leaders of Judea, come down to be seen where the actions at. Maybe to be baptized to seem holy. But John calls them out.

*O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come? Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance: And think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.And now also the axe is laid unto the root of the trees: therefore every tree which bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire.*

Much as Jesus would later, as detailed in Matthew 7 and 23, he calls out these hypocrites, this generation of vipers, false preachers who bear bad fruit. Not souls won, ready to accept Christ. They bring forth no fruit, thistles. False prophets, which come to you in sheep's clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves.

Then he goes after their reliance on being special boys, born from Abraham, saying God could make a rock a son of Abraham. That their being Jews isn't going to save them. (RIP Dispensationalism).

He tells these reprobate hypocrites that Jesus who's coming, will sort them like chafe from wheat, into the fire. Cut down their tree, throw it in the fire. Brimstone-throwing preaching. Amen!

And Jesus, our Lord comes, whose shoes we aren't worthy to unlatch. And he goes down into the water, and straightway rises up out of the water with the Holy Ghost upon Him. And the blessing of the Father is given to the Son. Amen.

teachings.title: The spirit of the Lord's supper, not the flesh
teachings.summary: How often a church observes the Lord's supper matters less than the spirit of it, and treating the physical bread and wine as a source of grace, as Rome and her offshoots do, is eating damnation.
teachings.text:
How various NT churches decide to engage in a Lord's supper together is really not important, so much the spirit by which it is done. Some do it in honor of the day leading to His death burial and resurrection. Some do it weekly. Some do it every meal they have at church or at home. I tend towards that, at least in the blessing and remembrance.

What isn't good doctrine is placing more in the physical eating and drinking than the spiritual application. Or placing it as a source for grace and salvation. The Catholic version of this and the Protestant spin offs have at their heart the wrong motives spiritually, and so eat and drink damnation unto themselves.

As Jesus says in **John 6**, *It is the spirit that quickeneth; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life.*

Those that heard and didn't understand this were offended and many disciples left from following Christ, because they took spiritual things literally, just as the Jews condemned Him for these "dark sayings."

teachings.title: No real presence, only remembrance
teachings.summary: There is no sacrament in the Lord's supper; believers remember Christ and give thanks whenever they eat together, and transubstantiation and real presence are neither taught nor hinted at.
teachings.text:
BTW if I wasn't clear, there is no sacramental aspect to this, no Lord's supper as it were, it's the meals we have together with other believers we're to remember Jesus, with the breaking of the bread and the drinking of the juice of the vine, or anything else that we eat together.

The idea of a real presence, or the Hocus pocus of a transubstantiation, is neither implied nor even hinted at. When two or three are gathered together in his name Jesus is there. He's always present. Our taking the time to remember him and thank God for the food, and acknowledging Christ's sacrifice for us it's just something we should do when we gather together.

People turning Christianity into a weird cannibal cult are the worst

teachings.title: Jethro's counsel to delegate judgment
teachings.summary: God approves delegated authority, so believers should know His word for themselves, with fathers, pastors and deacons answering to Christ, a pattern of the Millennial kingdom.
teachings.text:
But regardless of all that, and regardless of the marriage troubles Moses may have had, Jethro in his visit gives good advice to his son-in-law Moses.

Moses has 600,000 men, plus women and children in the mixed multitudes encamped with him. 12 tribes of Israel, come out of Egypt, and as their leader, he must sit in judgment. Jethro observes the long lines and the grind of dealing with them all that Moses faces and offers good advice.

*The thing that thou doest is not good.*
*Thou wilt surely wear away, both thou, and this people that is with thee: for this thing is too heavy for thee; thou art not able to perform it thyself alone.*
*Hearken now unto my voice, I will give thee counsel, and God shall be with thee: Be thou for the people to God-ward, that thou mayest bring the causes unto God: And thou shalt teach them ordinances and laws, and shalt shew them the way wherein they must walk, and the work that they must do. Moreover thou shalt provide out of all the people able men, such as fear God, men of truth, hating covetousness; and place such over them, to be rulers of thousands, and rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens: And let them judge the people at all seasons: and it shall be, that every great matter they shall bring unto thee, but every small matter they shall judge: so shall it be easier for thyself, and they shall bear the burden with thee. If thou shalt do this thing, and God command thee so, then thou shalt be able to endure, and all this people shall also go to their place in peace.*

God blesses this arrangement, and Moses takes to it and does as Jethro advised.

We see other times, in other places throughout the Bible that God approves of delegation of authority. He wants the people to know His ways and laws and the ordinances of remembrance, that in what they do they know the next right choice to make.

We are to know the word of God that we can know ourselves what His will is. Without needing someone micromanaging and interpreting scripture, to constantly make decisions for us on normal matters.

God then sets up captains over people, to judge matters for their people. By 10s, 100s and 1,000s. And a leader who answers to God, for the tougher matters of judgment. Thus will it be in the Millennium. Those who showed judgment and did great things for the Lord will be given much in the Kingdom. Those good and faithful servants will be made rulers, as Jesus described in the parable of the servants.

We see the wisdom in this arrangement. The way it maximizes the ability to serve God and edify people. And this exists today through God's word; the priesthood of believers, the husband/father of the home, the local pastor, his helpers the deacons or elders, all answering to Jesus. It is the form of Christian nationalism that we should seek.

teachings.title: Thyatira Suffered That Woman Jezebel to Teach
teachings.summary: Thyatira's troubles came from suffering a woman to teach against 1 Timothy 2:12, and Christ chastens such backslidden servants severely though they are saved.
teachings.text:
*And unto the angel of the church in Thyatira write; These things saith the Son of God, who hath his eyes like unto a flame of fire, and his feet are like fine brass;*

Again, writing now to Thyatira, Jesus as described in John's vision.

*I know thy works, and charity, and service, and faith, and thy patience, and thy works; and the last to be more than the first.*

The church at Thyatira is doing well, their works growing, the last more than the first. Patient, charitable, serving others, faithful.

*Notwithstanding I have a few things against thee, because thou sufferest that woman Jezebel, which calleth herself a prophetess, to teach and to seduce my servants to commit fornication, and to eat things sacrificed unto idols.*

But the Thyatirians have multiple problems, that all stem from allowing, suffering, a woman to teach.

**1 Timothy 2:12**:
*But I suffer not a woman to teach, nor to usurp authority over the man, but to be in silence.*

We see here exactly why this is a problem. Jezebel is joy only teaching, but in the authority she's gained over the men, has seduced them into fornication and to eat things sacrificed to idols. The error of Balaam compounded by her role in their church.

*And I gave her space to repent of her fornication; and she repented not. Behold, I will cast her into a bed, and them that commit adultery with her into great tribulation, except they repent of their deeds. And I will kill her children with death; and all the churches shall know that I am he which searcheth the reins and hearts: and I will give unto every one of you according to your works.*

By this passage, I assume Jezebel is actually a saved believer. That the sin she is in and leading others too comes from their disobeying God's word, and compounding the error, when given chance to repent and turn back towards God, she refused. Backslidden and defiant, Jesus says He will punish her and those who are with her. He chasteneth who He loves. These aren't some sort of reprobates like the Nicolaitanes, these are His servants gone astray.

And the punishment is severe. Casting her into bed, stricken sick. Likely of STDs. And those she misled into great tribulation, until they repent. He will even kill her children that the other churches will know the error that they were in, and His power, giving to each what they deserve that others may learn from their folly. We should all heed this warning, God is longsuffering but has His limits. He will repay us by our works, here on earth, even if we have been saved from Hell.

*But unto you I say, and unto the rest in Thyatira, as many as have not this doctrine, and which have not known the depths of Satan, as they speak; I will put upon you none other burden.*
*But that which ye have already hold fast till I come.* 

Jesus says to the rest of the congregation that haven't fallen into this wickedness to holdfast. Encouraging them that He will honor His promises to us at His return.

*And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations: And he shall rule them with a rod of iron; as the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers: even as I received of my Father. And I will give him the morning star. He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches.*

We who are saved and keep to His commands, doing the works He has asked of us, we will be rewarded by ruling and reigning over the Earth with Him in the millennial Kingdom. Ruling with a rod of iron, the perfect law of God. And we will receive the morning star, the glory that is Christ Jesus. Amen.

teachings.title: Pure religion: widows and the fatherless
teachings.summary: God commands care for widows and orphans, families must honour and support their own widows, and the church cares for widows indeed, a duty now largely handed to the state.
teachings.text:
*Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world*.
...
*Learn to do well; seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow.*
...
*He doth execute the judgment of the fatherless and widow, and loveth the stranger, in giving him food and raiment.*

There are two groups of people God has a special place for, and asks us to be protectors and caretakers of; widows and orphans.

This biblical appeal actually became a means by which many fraternal orders, Masonic lodges and other less than godly organizations worked a grift. Collecting donations for the "widows and orphans fund" became a euphemism for this kind of shakedown charity by the 20th Century. The idea itself synonymous with corruption. A punchline euphemism for illegal activities hidden under the guise of charity.

But in more recent decades, the concept, both Biblical and corrupt has all but disappeared, as the state welfare and entitlements has supplanted it. Now hardly any one, and sadly, few churches, give heed to the "pure religion" God commands us towards.

Here, in chapter 5 of first Timothy, Paul instructs the young evangelist on the proper church role and management for care of widows indeed.

Before getting to that, and continuing the thought of chapter 4 regarding Timothy's youth, and how to minimize those who look down on being told what to do by a younger man, Paul gives instruction. Don't rebuke an elder. Treat them as fathers, younger men as brothers, young girls as sisters (with a purity), and elderly women as mothers. This applies to us all, and our fellow congregants. We are family for Christ's sake, and as such have obligation for respect, and at times, honor.

Honor in the Bible has a financial aspect to it, that we give honor, payment, support, to our parents, is one of the main meanings behind the commandment. Giving honor to whom it is due is a point repeatedly made by God throughout the Bible, and this is the context of Paul's instructions here.

A widow indeed is one who, having lost her husband and not having sons or nephews (which means not only her siblings' children but grandchildren, and other younger relations), that these family members must honor her with support, that she not be a burden to the church. He warns;

*But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel.*

This is similar language to those facing church discipline laid out by Jesus, that they be put out from the congregation and treated as if they are unsaved. Heathens. Infidels.

teachings.title: Who is a widow indeed
teachings.summary: A widow indeed is over sixty, desolate, trusting God and devoted to good works, while younger widows should not be supported but remarry, lest idleness bring reproach on the church.
teachings.text:
Continuing, Paul lists more qualifiers for a widow "indeed," that she be desolate, trusteth in God, and continueth in supplications and prayers night and day. Poor, no means of support and giving her life to the faith, essentially. Further, he goes on to say she must be over 60, blameless and devoted to ministry of the church, and the wife of one man;

..*having been the wife of one man. Well reported of for good works; if she have brought up children, if she have lodged strangers, if she have washed the saints' feet, if she have relieved the afflicted, if she have diligently followed every good work.*

This makes her a true widow. A widow indeed.

Paul contrasts this with the exceptions. One who lives for pleasure rather than service is excluded, for example. And age is a factor;

*The younger widows refuse: for when they have begun to wax wanton against Christ, they will marry; Having damnation, because they have cast off their first faith. And withal they learn to be idle, wandering about from house to house; and not only idle, but tattlers also and busybodies, speaking things which they ought not.*

Young women, who could still remarry, shouldn't be given the honor by the church. Even if they swear they will be devoted to the ministry, and continuing in prayer, etc, Paul says they eventually will become wonton, that is, spoiled and pampered, having financial support with little to do all day but gossip and carry on, it will corrupt them, and eventually they will seek out a man to remarry, and make them abandon their first faith, that is that God will provide for them through the church that they are swearing devotion to, and leave for a husband. Damnation in this context means condemned by others for her behavior, not losing her salvation or going to Hell.

This is all true, we witness it ourselves today, especially with welfare taking the place of charity or family support. And frequently you may see at church a godly woman, coming from divorce or a husband's death, will put herself all in to helping out to keep herself busy, and eventually get married, often to an unsaved man, or worse, a man of the church she led to adultery and divorce, and her testimony becomes an open shame. Many such cases.

We see though out 1 Timothy, and other epistles but especially here, that the testimony to the unsaved by living blamelessly so that they may reach the lost with soul winning, is a top priority.

That they *give none occasion to the adversary to speak reproachfully.*

teachings.title: Let your women keep silence in the churches
teachings.summary: Women are to learn in silence in church under the pastor and ask their husbands at home, though they teach their children and share the gospel, and every member serves the same goal without pride in role.
teachings.text:
Paul notes, and it appears to be an issue in Corinth, that women in the church are to remain silent, so as to no usurp the authority of their husbands, and to protect the hierarchy God created, as enumerated in Chapter 11. This is not to say women cannot prophecy at all. They are called to teach scripture to their children, to convert their unbelieving husbands with their chaste conversation. We have multiple examples of women giving the Gospel and being active in spreading the word.

But in church, under the leadership of a man of God, the pastor, who has very specific qualifications listed in the pastoral epistles, they are to learn in silence, and in their questions to turn to their authority, their husbands or fathers, first.

As Paul had previously mentioned, each member of the body is important to the goal of the whole, and the "more important" parts shouldn't be puffed up, as they have reliance on the "uncomely" parts that serve the same head.

It isn't the role but the goal.

And we each have a responsibility to that larger goal, giving God the glory and increase of His harvest. And all who serve that goal shouldn't take pride in their role but humble themselves, which is the larger theme of this letter to Corinth.

teachings.title: Whited tombs: church as a checkbox
teachings.summary: Those who treat church and ritual as proof of holiness are whited tombs; we assemble to exhort one another and stay salty, praising God until Christ comes.
teachings.text:
God's accusations against them are sharp. They can tend with thieves and are partakers with adulterers. Both the literal engagement with the worldly, and the spiritual, of general ecumenicalism. They speak evil things, and lie. They not only don't love their neighbors, but they lie against their own brothers.

And God, God who is longsuffering and merciful and wood that all men come to repentance, gave them space and time to reconsider their ways. Instead they considered themselves holy, like God is Holy. They thought that in their religious practices, and keeping the letter of the law that they could ignore the purpose of the law and its spirit.

It's the same indictment here as in **Matthew 23**. And it could be said Of so many supposed Christians today.

It's interesting to me that **Hebrews 10** bookends the idea of being no more need for sacrifice for those in Christ, and there being no more sacrifice for willful sin, around the command to attend church.

**Hebrews 10:23–25**
*Let us hold fast the profession of our faith without wavering; (for he is faithful that promised;) And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works: Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching.*

We are commanded to not forsake the assembly. And the purpose of that is to love one another. Edifying each other. Building each other up. So much more as the day approaches.

But today, there are those who see church as a check box for their righteousness. Proving that they are holy as God is holy simply by their attendance. And in so many acts that they do, they wash the outside of the vessel, while inside they are whited tombs filled with dead men's bones.

Those people to whom religion is a series of rituals and obligations that only benefit themselves, who see sacraments as their sacrifice rather than the blood of Christ. Christians in name only who go through the motions and never once consider God.

They forget God and he will tear them to pieces. They bury their talent out of fear, while never truly fearing God.

But God, ever gracious ends on a positive note.

*Whoso offereth praise glorifieth me: and to him that ordereth his conversation aright will I shew the salvation of God.*

Our purpose of being his people is to praise his name that he be glorified among men. We are the salt of the earth. We are what is preserving the world against judgment. And so he's encouraging us to continue in that praise and thanksgiving and glorifying God among men.

Because it is possible for salt to lose its savor. For lukewarm Christians to have the candle of their church put out. To be of no further use of God so he calls you home if you're saved and if you're not, casting you into outer darkness.

**Matthew 5:13**
*Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out, and to be trodden under foot of men.*

God's case against Israel is God's case against all who call themselves by His name and fail to live to proclaim His glory.

Let us then stay salty, maintain our savor, do all things with Mercy and judgment forgiving those who trespass against us, considering the plight of the poor and the widow and the fatherless. Exhorting one another.

So that at the coming of Christ, when He brings firey judgment upon the world, We will be found acceptable. Where He will say that we are good and faithful servants. Amen

teachings.title: No want to them that fear Him
teachings.summary: God provides for those who fear Him and live righteously, chastens those who do not, and expects believers to love the brethren by not forsaking the assembling of the local church.
teachings.text:
*O fear the LORD, ye his saints: for there is no want to them that fear him.*

Believers, sanctified in the Spirit by faith in the risen Christ, are given the promise that the Lord will redeem us, His servants.

But His provision for us extends beyond the fact of eternal salvation, and gives us hope and comfort here, in this life. Our daily bread, shelter, clothing, we shall not want for any good thing.

But more, He's given us His word, and His standards for separation that we may fear the Lord and be blessed by having a longer life and see good within the years we are allotted.

His burden is light. Don't speak evil of others, don't lie. Don't seek to harm others, but do good and seek peace.

**Romans 12:18**
*If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.*

Vengeance is Mine, sayeth the Lord. He will repay. We not only believe He is, and a rewarder of those that diligently seek Him, but that He is our shield and strength against our enemies. We do not need to fight a battle, but trust in Him to fight for us. We simply need to walk in the Spirit, love our enemies, hate His, and seek others' profit. Doing good.

If we want our Father's blessing, live righteously. He hears the righteous and answers their cry.

We are known by our love for the brethren. By our edifying one another.

**Hebrews 10:22–25**
*Let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and our bodies washed with pure water. Let us hold fast the profession of our faith without wavering; (for he is faithful that promised;) And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works: Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching.*

You don't want the face of God against you in your time of need.

**Hebrews 10:26–29**
*For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins, But a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation, which shall devour the adversaries. He that despised Moses’ law died without mercy under two or three witnesses: Of how much sorer punishment, suppose ye, shall he be thought worthy, who hath trodden under foot the Son of God, and hath counted the blood of the covenant, wherewith he was sanctified, an unholy thing, and hath done despite unto the Spirit of grace?*

God will chasten His children. He will shorten your life and withhold blessings, and even bring you home for not doing His work at His pleasure.

**Hebrews 10:31**
*It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.*

Note that we are expected to love and care for our fellow saints. And where do we do this? On the called out assembly of believers. Our local church. Forsaking this opportunity is spiteful to the Spirit of grace which has bought you. Go to church!

teachings.title: Sing skilfully with instruments and doctrine
teachings.summary: Scripture commands singing with instruments in the congregation, songs full of doctrine, avoiding both carnal rock-concert worship and the removal of instruments.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 33** opens with the clearest enforcement of writing, singing and performing songs of praise and worship to Almighty God. On stringed instruments, especially. Performing skillfully and with a loud noise within the congregation, songs with the doctrine of scripture, with the truth of His mighty works being honored.

God's righteousness and judgment, His power and creation, the fear and adoration He commands from those that love the Lord to sing unto Him.

Book of Psalms explicitly names several musical instruments, including the harp, psaltery, timbrel, cymbal, trumpet, cornet, organ, and pipe. These are given instructions by the Psalmist and the music leader, and are used to provide melody and concordance to the congregational singing. An activity that we are encouraged to perform in the New Testament church.

**Colossians 3:16**
*Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord.*

Music is a form of learning and worship, as much as prayer, and it is edifying to the soul when focused on this spiritual truth, that it is for His sake that we make melodies.

**Ephesians 5:19**
*Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord*

What it is not, is an excuse to be carnal, to satisfy the flesh with worldly beats and discordant instruments, mimicking a rock concert or depraved discotheque.

Congregational singing stirs the soul, lifting your voice up to the Lord. But many worship services turn into a tantric trance, lifting up hands and swaying, captivated by the music and beats, lasting hours at some churches. With songs that are thinly veiled pop love songs, with little to no doctrine applied.

Other churches take the instruments completely out of the equation, which seems at odds with the details given in the Bible.

There is a middle ground, and a place for various musical accompaniments, while maintaining the orderly and decent service that all things at church should be done in.

teachings.title: In the midst of the congregation will I praise thee
teachings.summary: Trials are an opportunity to overcome by God's power and praise Him among the brethren, which cannot be done by forsaking the assembly.
teachings.text:
Psalm 22 continues. The desperate plea of the condemned man, compassed by dogs, scorned and ridiculed, pierced and heartbroken, feeling abandoned by God, turns to a prayer of certain hope.

We know God has delivered every promise He has made. He has heard the cries of His people and, in due season, saved them.

We may persist in our prayers, reminding God, and ourselves, of His faithfulness, as we ask for more immediate relief. His perfect timing may not be ours, but at our weakest He shows His strength.

*Deliver my soul from the sword; my darling from the power of the dog. Save me from the lion’s mouth: for thou hast heard me from the horns of the unicorns.*

From the proverbial horns of a dilemma, from the immediate threat, we call upon the name of the Lord. Not only the saved, His darling, but the lost often find His strength in their time of trial. Foxhole converts.

The Potter often moves the clay in such a way, that we finally see our shortcomings and impotency, and need His hand to lift us up, that we may be what He has planned for us to become.

If even Jesus Christ was to be made a reproach and murdered by bloody men in a wicked act, that we may know eternal life, as the risen and triumphant Son of God, then our trials are an opportunity to overcome by His power and to give the Lord the glory.

*I will declare thy name unto my brethren: in the midst of the congregation will I praise thee.*

In the midst of tribulation, we shall praise Him. That is the mind of a mature Christian. It is difficult to see, sometimes, and we may feel isolated, alone, but in our most desperate hour, we praise Him. We declare His holy name to our brethren, in the congregation we hold up His excellence.

(It may not be a primary (or even secondary) application of this psalm, but it strikes me that we cannot lift up our voice in praise to the congregation, to declare His name unto the brethren, if we avoid church. If we forsake the assembly. Go to church!)

teachings.title: The vineyard let out to keepers
teachings.summary: Where Israel's husbandmen betrayed the Lord's vineyard, the bride freely gives Him its fruit and pays the keepers, as believers support pastors and missionaries with tithes and offerings.
teachings.text:
Then a parable of her beloved, the lord Solomon, and his vineyard. He let, or leased it out to keepers, to be dressed. And their charge was a thousand pieces of silver, purchased by the fruit they would harvest.

The same is the vineyards of Christ's parables. The talents of silver. The harvest and the increase. The unprofitable servants of Israel, the wicked keepers who slew the prophets and even the Son of the Lord. The spiritual understanding that comes from knowing this first; the Lord planted a vineyard;

**Isaiah 5:1–7**
*Now will I sing to my wellbeloved a song of my beloved touching his vineyard. My wellbeloved hath a vineyard in a very fruitful hill: And he fenced it, and gathered out the stones thereof, and planted it with the choicest vine, and built a tower in the midst of it, and also made a winepress therein: and he looked that it should bring forth grapes, and it brought forth wild grapes. And now, O inhabitants of Jerusalem, and men of Judah, judge, I pray you, betwixt me and my vineyard. What could have been done more to my vineyard, that I have not done in it? wherefore, when I looked that it should bring forth grapes, brought it forth wild grapes? And now go to; I will tell you what I will do to my vineyard: I will take away the hedge thereof, and it shall be eaten up; and break down the wall thereof, and it shall be trodden down: And I will lay it waste: it shall not be pruned, nor digged; but there shall come up briers and thorns: I will also command the clouds that they rain no rain upon it. For the vineyard of the LORD of hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah his pleasant plant: and he looked for judgment, but behold oppression; for righteousness, but behold a cry.*

The woman offers her vineyard to Solomon, pledging the tribute of a thousand, and even the keepers, a wage of two hundred. Pledging her fruit to her Lord.

The Lord planted and cultivated a vineyard with Israel, and the husband men betrayed Him. But the woman, as the faithful believer willingly offers herself as a vineyard, and freely gives the Lord His tribute. The fruit we gather. The works we do for the cause of the gospel. She gladly pays the workers a wage. Just as we do with tithes and offerings to sustain our pastors, our churches, ministries and missionaries, that work in the fields for God.

teachings.title: Meddle not with them that are given to change
teachings.summary: Change for its own sake has led churches into apostasy, from Catholicism to modernism and the compromise of standards and music, and moving the landmarks of the fathers ends in sudden ruin.
teachings.text:
*My son, fear thou the Lord and the king: and meddle not with them that are given to change: For their calamity shall rise suddenly; and who knoweth the ruin of them both?*

The people who promote change as an end to itself, that we must "progress," to leave the old paths to strike out in the new, covet ideas of what they think could be, because they don't appreciate what is.

In Christianity, this has resulted in more tragedy and departure from the Biblical truth found in the fear of the Lord. Taking His word as the final authority.

Denominational control was a reaction to the fact that some churches fell into apostasy. This gave us the false religion of Catholicism.

In recent times, the 19th and 20th century were plagued by modernism and changing of God's word to justify it. Even in the past few decades, churches that had resisted change and kept the right gospel, began to compromise with the world to "keep up with the times." Dropping standards, adding carnal appeals in music, technology, dress, "worship," to attract younger crowds.

But the ruin of these changes comes suddenly. You can only go so far afield, and drift off the well-worn paths so far without finding yourself in sudden calamity. You can't move the landmarks of your fathers' and not become lost.

teachings.title: Gravity before office, not after
teachings.summary: Deacons and respected men must already be grave and sober before they are named, so young Christian men should put away the world's arrested development and seek sobriety, humble service and kindness.
teachings.text:
**1 Timothy 3:8-13**
*Likewise must the deacons be grave, not doubletongued, not given to much wine, not greedy of filthy lucre; Holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience. And let these also first be proved; then let them use the office of a deacon, being found blameless. Even so must their wives be grave, not slanderers, sober, faithful in all things. Let the deacons be the husbands of one wife, ruling their children and their own houses well. For they that have used the office of a deacon well purchase to themselves a good degree, and great boldness in the faith which is in Christ Jesus*

Many men in Christ today say, "well I am not a pastor. I don't have to do much, I can coast on helping with chairs after the service. The deacons and elders at the church have always been there. They do the heavy lifting."

Respected men of faith in the church don't put on this gravity like a coat when they get named. It isn't a longevity award. You must be these things before you are ever even considered for leadership. And it should be your guide and goal as a young man.

The world has made arrested development into a virtue. Being unserious as a way to comport yourself. This retards the growth of a Christian man.

We see it in ourselves, certainly. An immaturity that must be tamed and brought under control. It's fine to joke and laugh, but in its place. Sobriety and gravity are what we should strive for, coupled with grace and mercy for those who have no one to deliver them.

With kindness as the goal. Not lordship.

Like Job, respect that comes from putting on God's righteousness and judgment. From living out your faith. You gain respect and influence by being a doer of the word, by being a humble servant. Not a prideful boaster.

In chapter 32 we will meet a young man, Elihu, who we will see is offended by Job's defense, and seeks to have respect given him, the wrong way. But for now we should reflect on Job's example, and the application for our own lives.

teachings.title: Be pure of the blood of all men
teachings.summary: Everyone can spare a few hours a week to go soul-winning with a church, so warn souls rather than pass by the burning house.
teachings.text:
I know it weighs heavy on my heart the number of people I have passed on giving the gospel too. The regret of hearing someone you know died, that you never warned. Feeling that blood on your head. I think every Christian, even babes in Christ, have had this feeling.

"Oh, how I wish I had warned them!" is a common lament.

How much more then should we feel that burden when we don't go soul-winning? When given a church, an opportunity to door knock, and we don't go?

It's one thing to wake to a fire in your own house, and warn your family to flee. But if you passed the home of strangers, and saw a fire spreading, wouldn't you bang on the door to get them to evacuate?

Or would you pass on by, leaving them to burn?

We cannot reach everyone. It would be difficult to quit our jobs, abandon our family and make evangelizing the world out only purpose. But everyone can spare a few hours a week to go soul-winning.

If you aren't part of a church, join one, even if it is for this sole purpose.

Organized door knocking is more profitable, and having a place to send the souls won to be taught all things and be baptized is crucial.

If you go to church, and they don't have soul-winning, ask the pastor to start a program. Offer to organize it. There are faithful people who would make excellent watchmen, sitting on the sidelines for lack of a program.

Warn souls. Be pure of the blood of all men.

teachings.title: All things come of Thee: giving willingly
teachings.summary: Beyond the tithe, all we have is God's, so we should give to the church, the brethren and missions cheerfully and willingly with thanksgiving.
teachings.text:
Here in **1 Chronicles 29**, the final chapter, we come to the transition of power between King David and his son Solomon. David has, in obedience to the Lord, organized the Kingdom, set up the leaders of men and the chain of command in the various roles and responsibilities. He has given Solomon the plans for the house of God, the pattern given by the Spirit, and laid up treasure and provisions to see it built.

And the people all willingly gave treasure to build up the house of the Lord and to do His work. Free will offerings.

David calls them to prayer and to bless the Lord God of Israel, to give Him all glory and honor. David's prayer reminds us that whatever we give to the service of God is His to begin with.

Tithing, the practice of giving the first of the flock, the tenth of the wealth and harvest, etc...these are commands in the Old Testament, that we honor today in the New.

But the free will offerings here are a reminder that all we have *cometh of Thine hand, and is all Thine own.* Not just 10%, pretax income, itemized and listed on our taxes. All of it. Everything we have is His because it is by His grace we have it at all.

For all things come of God. And when we give, it is of God's own.

When we approach giving towards the church, or to help the brethren, or missions and church plants and soul winning trips...whatever it may be, give cheerfully, willingly.

Because riches and honor come from God. It is His power to make us great, and blessed by whatever riches He provides. We can't take it with us; there are none abiding.

So give joyfully, knowing it's not yours but the Lord's. And rejoice in it, praising Him in thanksgiving, that you have abundance wherewithal to give.

teachings.title: Delivered unto Satan, yet the spirit saved
teachings.summary: God uses Satan to chasten His people, and Paul's delivering the Corinthian fornicator to Satan for the destruction of the flesh that the spirit be saved teaches once saved always saved.
teachings.text:
This is a story of David we covered back during the study on [2 Samuel 24](https://t.me/HouseOfWews2/14351)

The difference between the versions is slight, but the added detail gives us perspective. In **2 Samuel 24**, we are told;

*And again the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel, and he moved David against them to say, Go, number Israel and Judah.*

Here, in **1 Chronicles 21** we get more understanding;

*And Satan stood up against Israel, and provoked David to number Israel.*

Just like Job, often God uses Satan to tempt us that we may be chastened, corrected and brought to repentance or, sadly, fail and condemn ourselves further.

**1 Corinthians 5:4-5**
*In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, when ye are gathered together, and my spirit, with the power of our Lord Jesus Christ, To deliver such an one unto Satan for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord Jesus.*

We see this in the case of the fornication going on in the church at Corinth, where a man among them is chambering with his father's widow. Not only fornication, but an abomination.

Paul tells them to church discipline him, that he be given over to Satan for destruction of the flesh, even if his spirit is saved. God allows Satan to destroy us in the flesh. The hope in church discipline is that the person gets right. Sees their error and comes back. But if not, at least in death they are free from the sin and present with the Lord.

Note this teaches OSAS.

Please follow the link to the previous study where I break down the sin of numbering the people in a way other than how God intended.

teachings.title: The great commission is a command
teachings.summary: Rather than ignoring the warnings, chasing hidden knowledge or hiding away, believers are to assemble together all the more and preach the gospel to every creature before the judgment comes.
teachings.text:
**1 Corinthians 10:11**
*Now all these things happened unto them for examples: and they are written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come.*

When Jesus came to the world as the son of man, it was not as the prophets of old. *For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved.*

His mission was to show there is peace and goodwill available with the Father, to preach repentance and salvation, grace and mercy to heal the sinner and gather the lost.

But, even in that, as he neared the cross, Christ preached hard against the sin of the Pharisees and the Jews, their destruction to come for the blood of the prophets, and the blood of Christ that they would shed.

The other prophets that came before Christ preached wrath and destruction, of His coming and salvation, but never a man spoke as He did.

But, most of the prophecy of the wrath of His judgment, Jesus gave warning through John, in Revelation.

Today, many ignore the warnings outright. Some argue endlessly about the details, claiming knowledge and insight about the people and events, ascribing to current political and religious leaders traits of the beast and Babylon, and still more choose to believe the hey will be taken out of the way before Tribulation comes, and so they check out, and miss the point for believers.

We are to preach the same message of salvation, mercy and grace to every creature. To share the gospel far and wide. Not to hunker down in fear, in remote villages, or cabins in the woods. Not to dwell in chat rooms and online platforms seeking "hidden knowledge."

We are to gather together, in real life, even more so as the hour draws nigh;

**Hebrews 10:24-25**
*And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works: Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching.*

And let us share the good news of salvation in Christ to every creature, now before the judgment comes.

*And he said unto them, Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature.*

The great commission is a command.

*The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised, To preach the acceptable year of the Lord.*

teachings.title: Micah's house of gods and the Danites' apostate priest
teachings.summary: Dan conquered Laish with Micah's stolen idols and a hired Levite priest, sowing its own downfall into captivity, a picture of Rome's idols, images and unqualified priesthood that God will judge.
teachings.text:
**Joshua 19:47**
*And the coast of the children of Dan went out too little for them: therefore the children of Dan went up to fight against Leshem, and took it, and smote it with the edge of the sword, and possessed it, and dwelt therein, and called Leshem, Dan, after the name of Dan their father.*

**Judges 17-18** tells the story of Micah, his creation of his own church full of idols and icons, an ephod and teraphim, and his recruiting of a young Levite to be his personal house priest, calling him "father."

In those days there was no king in Israel. And men did as seemed right in their own eyes.

The story presented occurs during the period immediately after Joshua's death, where Dan had not fully gone out to take their inheritance from those that dwelled there.

**Joshua 23:4-5**
*Behold, I have divided unto you by lot these nations that remain, to be an inheritance for your tribes, from Jordan, with all the nations that I have cut off, even unto the great sea westward. And the LORD your God, he shall expel them from before you, and drive them from out of your sight; and ye shall possess their land, as the LORD your God hath promised unto you.*

Joshua had waxed old and died before the tribes had finished the work to go out and possess the land given them. Dan especially was shown to be dragging behind the other tribes.

And here they are seeking to go out and find land to take. In **Judges 18**, we find that the troop of spies stop at Mt Ephraim, and lodge at the house of Micah. There they recognized the young Levite, and inquire why he's there. He tells them of the arrangements made with Micah, his hire and role as a private priest over a house of gods.

They ask him for God's blessings in finding a suitable city to take, and he says reassuring words that God had blessed their endeavors. And so, 600 Danites set forth to go into the land, armed for war.

They come up on the house of Micah and the spies tell their army about the gods and the silver graven image and the ephod and priest, and they go in and take all the idols and ephod for themselves. The priest protests and they tell him to come with them and be their priest, and he agrees.

Micah seeing this runs out with some men from his town and Micah confronts them. The much larger force of men gathered for war tell him to stop, or he may forfeit his and his family's lives.

And so Dan finds the city of Laish, or Leshem, and the people there living simple and peaceful lives, and take it for themselves, renaming the city Dan.

And the young priest of the Levites turns out to be the son of Gershom, he and his sons, with their stolen idols and icons and fake Ephod, become the priests for the tribe of Dan until the captivity of the land. The seeds of their own downfall sown by rejecting the way of the Lord and turning to idols.

A people can seem mighty, and put many simple peasants to the sword while carrying the banner of conquest, and relying on idols and images. Unqualified priests. But in the end, God will judge them and their abominations.

Danites went marching on a crusade with their apostate priest and easily took the land, but lost their understanding. The parallel with Roman Catholics should be obvious. The end of those people being captivity and destruction, if they don't turn from Idolatry, repenting towards the Lord.

teachings.title: The gift of helps
teachings.summary: The gift of helps or ministry is serving one another as members of one body, as Paul praised his fellow laborers in Romans 16.
teachings.text:
**Mark 9:35**
*And he sat down, and called the twelve, and saith unto them, If any man desire to be first, the same shall be last of all, and servant of all*.

In discussing the gifts of the Spirit given to believers as part of the body of Christ, Paul mentions "helps;"

**1 Corinthians 12:28**
*And God hath set some in the church, first apostles, secondarily prophets, thirdly teachers, after that miracles, then gifts of healings, helps, governments, diversities of tongues.*

In **Romans 12:4-16**, it's ministry, but the same concept, those helping others to edify the whole body, as servants towards one another;

*For as we have many members in one body, and all members have not the same office: So we, being many, are one body in Christ, and every one members one of another. Having then gifts differing according to the grace that is given to us, whether prophecy, let us prophesy according to the proportion of faith*; *Or ministry, let us wait on our ministering: or he that teacheth, on teaching; Or he that exhorteth, on exhortation: he that giveth, let him do it with simplicity; he that ruleth, with diligence; he that sheweth mercy, with cheerfulness.*

*Let love be without dissimulation. Abhor that which is evil; cleave to that which is good. Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love; in honour preferring one another; Not slothful in business; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord; Rejoicing in hope; patient in tribulation; continuing instant in prayer; Distributing to the necessity of saints; given to hospitality. Bless them which persecute you: bless, and curse not. Rejoice with them that do rejoice, and weep with them that weep. Be of the same mind one toward another. Mind not high things, but condescend to men of low estate. Be not wise in your own conceits.*

And just as **Romans 16** ends with Paul praising those fellow laborers in the ministry of the gospel, immortalizing the saints who'd helped him, he thanks others throughout the epistles for their help. Their willingness to serve the larger body. To condescend to those of lower prominence, that they may benefit from the charitable love which is the fruit of the Spirit within us.

teachings.title: Seek to be a help in the church
