teachings.summary: Helping is the most neglected gift, so we should come to church looking to be a blessing and serve with cheer.
teachings.text:
I could do a week's worth of posts from scripture that teaches this simple doctrine, one that is so badly overlooked, being the less comely of the gifts. And though it is the easiest of the gifts to be manifest in a believer, it is often the most neglected, the least coveted, the one responsibility so many shirk. (Of which I am chief...)

If all parts of the body are equally important in serving the head, which is Christ, and not being a respecter of persons is a command, then we should diligently seek the ability to be a help to others. To show up to church, not to feed our own needs, being wise in our own conceits, but looking whereby we can be a blessing. Asking what needs be done, with cheer. Rejoicing in our liberty that we have the opportunity to be a help to the Kingdom of God itself.

Seek to emulate those mentioned in the epistles as great helpers of the gospel, who minister the saints.

teachings.title: Speaking in tongues was known languages
teachings.summary: Tongues at Pentecost were real foreign languages for spreading the gospel, and Paul's tongues of angels is a hypothetical, not a doctrine.
teachings.text:
Speaking in tongues is described in Acts as the miracle of the disciples present on Pentecost, going out to the crowds of the feast in Jerusalem, and giving the gospel to those gathered from every nation in their own tongues. Their languages.

Judeans and Samaritans, who knew Aramaic, Greek. Hebrew, suddenly were speaking Parthian, and Mede, and Elamite, and Mesopotamian, and Phrygian, and Pamphylian, Egyptian, and Libyan and Latin, and a host of other languages, of all the scattered Israelites and others, gathered there that day. Prophesying the word of God and preaching the risen Christ.

This gift of the Holy Ghost continued in the early church, as it grew and served as a sign that brought the gospel to every nation, tongue and kindred. The God who had divided the nations and confused the languages in Babel, uniting them through the miraculous gifts of speaking in, and as we see in Corinthians, understanding or interpretation. Allowing them to be understood and to understand, that the gospel would be preached.

Even today, absent miracles but by the same grace, the same gift is given many who are quick studies in understanding languages, and given to allow the furtherance of the Gospel, bringing many to Christ.

The men in the church of Corinth, blessed with the more suspense gift, were puffed up, showing off, in the church. This was not only causing contention within the church, but as Paul says, gave a bad report to those without, that they were all babbling madmen. He admonishes them in Chapter 13 to seek rather Charity, the unfeigned and gracious love of others. Their profit and welfare. Their edification. Not our own.

And in the case of being able to speak in a tongue foreign to others, it serves no one but the speaker.

*Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal...For he that speaketh in an unknown tongue speaketh not unto men, but unto God: for no man understandeth him; howbeit in the spirit he speaketh mysteries. But he that prophesieth speaketh unto men to edification, and exhortation, and comfort. He that speaketh in an unknown tongue edifieth himself; but he that prophesieth edifieth the church.*

This is the sum of what Paul is teaching. He uses the idea that *even if* he were to speak in the language of angels, if no one understands it, it is useless, even to the speaker. Paul is not saying that they *are* speaking the language of angels. It is a hypothetical exaggeration given for instruction.

That some make an entire doctrine from that goes to show that those who wrest with scripture do so to their own destruction, because in the same scripture lays the context and the truth.

teachings.title: Pride turns the gifts into doctrine
teachings.summary: False churches made the list of gifts primary doctrine out of pride and covetousness, and gifted men can use knowledge, governance or preaching for their own prominence.
teachings.text:
So. Knowing this, the list of examples given by Paul becomes incidental to the overall message. But in some false churches, the list became primary doctrine, and this heresy took hold precisely because of these sins in the hearts of men.

Wanting to feel powerful, special, better than. Given over to jealousy and vainglory. Coveting the attention and respect of persons given to those who are talented in some of the more prominent and manifest ways.

And so you have churches that place the expression of "spiritual gifts," as a witness to the "faith" of the person holding them. Of how special God must think they are, and wanting that for themselves.

Now, knowledge and wisdom are given every man his measure, by walking in the Spirit and study of the word, and from that the skill of preaching and teaching. And some will be puffed up, taking the gift of intelligence and time, studying to be approved by men, rather than God.

They use their knowledge to gain respect and power of others. And they guard dispensing it, rather than giving it freely as it was given them. They make themselves feel superior to others, and often seek to control those that they impress, rather than edifying others with humility and longsuffering. Their heart isn't right.

And some take their gifts for governance; organizational talents and judgement, and in pride make it about themselves, and their own power and prominence, not in glory to God.

And many take their ability to prophesy, preaching with great oration, and using that to gain a following and preeminence among the brethren.

The more comely parts thinking themselves better than the less comely but equally important parts.

And the less comely, envying and resenting the comely.

teachings.title: Ordinances a memorial of Christ
teachings.summary: The offerings pictured Christ as the Lord's supper memorializes Him, ordinances having no power themselves, and the stranger always had the same salvation by faith.
teachings.text:
**Numbers 15** veers back to the clarification of the law, in this chapter, the ordinances of sacrifice, the meat offerings which includes the lambs or goats, which contain the blood of the testament between God and the Israelites, but also the flour and oil, which is made bread and wine, the juice of the vine.

Just as Jesus is the lamb slain for our sins, and His body broken like bread for our transgressions, and the cup offered as the blood of the new and better testament between God and man.

Ordinances are a memorial. They themselves have no power, and aren't the thing itself, but a picture of that thing, so too are the sacrifices given Moses a picture of Christ to come. Given us, as the Lord's supper, in remembrance of the risen Christ Jesus. That whenever it is done, we memorialize His work and the promise of God, until Jesus returns.

And we see that the stranger among the Israelites would be given the same ordinance, for the same memorial, of the same faith. There is no Jew or Greek.

God is not a respecter of persons. The salvation offered by faith was always available to whosoever will. To those that call upon the name of the Lord. Before there was Abraham. Before the circumcision. Before Jacob birthed Israel. Before the giving of the law at Sinai. The promise of salvation was given to all who called upon the name of the Lord, and they were made sons of God.

Israel was meant to be a beacon, to draw all men to repentance that they could participate in the supper table of the Lamb. But in their failing, God lifted up Jesus that all men be called that some might be saved. Amen.

teachings.title: Hair length and the order of heads
teachings.summary: In 1 Corinthians 11 the woman's covering is her long hair, as a man's long hair is a shame, under God's order of heads: Christ, the man, the woman.
teachings.text:
**1 Corinthians 11:1-16**
 *Be ye followers of me, even as I also am of Christ. Now I praise you, brethren, that ye remember me in all things, and keep the ordinances, as I delivered them to you. But I would have you know, that the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God. Every man praying or prophesying, having his head covered, dishonoureth his head. But every woman that prayeth or prophesieth with her head uncovered dishonoureth her head: for that is even all one as if she were shaven. For if the woman be not covered, let her also be shorn: but if it be a shame for a woman to be shorn or shaven, let her be covered.*

*For a man indeed ought not to cover his head, forasmuch as he is the image and glory of God: but the woman is the glory of the man.*

*For the man is not of the woman: but the woman of the man. Neither was the man created for the woman; but the woman for the man. For this cause ought the woman to have power on her head because of the angels.*

 *Nevertheless neither is the man without the woman, neither the woman without the man, in the Lord. For as the woman is of the man, even so is the man also by the woman; but all things of God.*

*Judge in yourselves: is it comely that a woman pray unto God uncovered? Doth not even nature itself teach you, that, if a man have long hair, it is a shame unto him? But if a woman have long hair, it is a glory to her: for her hair is given her for a covering.*

*But if any man seem to be contentious, we have no such custom, neither the churches of God.*

Just to be clear, the woman being uncovered means shorn, her hair cut short to the scalp with a razor. Some take it to mean a hat or veil, but the context here is a man with long hair in the church being a dishonorable thing, just as a woman shorn or shaven.

People get hung up in the slight diversion Paul takes to establish the order of "heads," the hierarchy that the woman is of the man and the man of Christ's, that we are all under God. The "head" in this regard is not the physical body part but the ruler. The higher power each submits to. And the "because of the angels" line seems like a non sequitur, or an instruction that if a woman doesn't put a hat on when praying the angels have a problem with it. It is a line that is open to some interpretation, but the larger point is hair length, and that can be discerned by the surrounding text.

My thoughts are that in giving the hierarchy, a woman is subject unto the man because of Eve and the temptation of Satan, an angel, and the curse put upon Eve in the garden.

**Genesis 3:16**
*Unto the woman he said, I will greatly multiply thy sorrow and thy conception; in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children; and thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.*

But that's just my opinion.

teachings.title: Without the camp: uncleanness a picture of sin
teachings.summary: Putting the unclean outside the camp pictures church discipline, putting sin out of our lives, and separation from the world.
teachings.text:
Chapter 5 of Numbers is divided into three sections, highlighted by God restating or clarifying previous commands given in Exodus and Leviticus, and adding another, the law of jealousy.

First, God reiterates the law of the unclean, those with leprosy, issues which means blood issues, sores or boils, or other kinds of sickness that causes the body to release fluids, and those unclean having come in contact with the dead. That these people be put without the camp that their uncleanliness doesn't affect others.

We have already read these things and the timing of the exile. Leprosy being contagious and generally incurable, the person would be permanently removed, although a ritual with the Levites and a method for determining they be clean if healed was laid out in **Leviticus 14:1-9** (covered [here](https://t.me/HouseOfWews2/9168) and [here](https://t.me/HouseOfWews2/11251))

Issues potentially carrying some kind of contagious disease, withdrawn until it has cleared or they are healed. We see a woman with blood issues her whole life healed by simply touching the hem of Jesus' cloak in **Luke 8:43-48**.

The law about being unclean by the touching of a carcase was given against the Levites with general instructions and is mentioned here, with more specific rules given in **Numbers 19:11**;
*The one who touches the corpse of any person shall be unclean for seven days.*...With purification rituals attached.

Physically they are instructions to keep diseases from spreading. To stop outbreaks of illness that could spread from person to person. Spiritually, all are a picture of sin, and the exile similar to church discipline, the removal of leaven that can spoil a whole lump.

It also pictures the removal of our own sin in our lives, that can grow and metastasize until we are castaway in our backslidden state. Useless to the Lord.

You can also see how it pictures separation from the world, keeping the unclean from that which is holy, the temple of God within us, where the holy Spirit dwells; that *shall ye put out, without the camp shall ye put them; that they defile not their camps, in the midst whereof I dwell.*

We should be mindful of these applications, understanding that the physical revelation of the Old Testament carries with them the spiritual applications for our lives as Christians today.

teachings.title: The Lord's supper versus Catholic communion
teachings.summary: Since God forbids eating blood and Jesus called the cup the fruit of the vine, the Lord's supper is a remembrance and the Catholic mass is a pagan perversion.
teachings.text:
In **Leviticus 17**, God reiterates His command that the children of Israel not consume blood. As we see from **Genesis 9** and **Acts 15**, this command predates the Levitical laws, and extends to the New Testament, where believers are told to not only abstain from consuming blood, but also food offered to idols.

The blood, the life thereof, *whosoever eateth it shall be cut off.*

We see in the ordinance of the Lord's supper, the remembrance of Christ's death and the new testament of His blood shed for the remission of sin.

**Matthew 26:26-29**
*And as they were eating, Jesus took bread, and blessed it, and brake it, and gave it to the disciples, and said, Take, eat; this is my body. And he took the cup, and gave thanks, and gave it to them, saying, Drink ye all of it; For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins. But I say unto you, I will not drink henceforth of this fruit of the vine, until that day when I drink it new with you in my Father's kingdom.*

Now, knowing that the consumption of blood is an abomination to the Lord, cutting off someone from being a child of Israel, and that the law against it is not done away with the end of the Levitical ceremonial laws and ordinances, predating them, and being commanded by the apostles to the Gentiles, is there a contradiction?

Since God is not the author of confusion, and Jesus Himself says that this cup is still just grape juice after His blessing, *this fruit of the vine*, no.

It is a form of materialist literalism that has a false doctrine that the bread literally turns to flesh and the juice literally becomes blood when their priests offer up wine and crackers to idols. The Catholic hocus pocus is Nicodemus-level in missing the spiritual application and meaning, to turn Christianity into a cannibal cult.

In the Catholic religion, they call the offering of the bread and alcoholic wine, lifted up to graven images "a sacrifice." They pray to their idol that it be acceptable as a sacrifice. They consume meat offered to idols, and in their hearts, consume what they will claim is blood.

It is a wicked pagan perversion of what should be a simple remembrance:

**Luke 22:14-20**
*And when the hour was come, he sat down, and the twelve apostles with him. And he said unto them, With desire I have desired to eat this passover with you before I suffer: For I say unto you, I will not any more eat thereof, until it be fulfilled in the kingdom of God. And he took the cup, and gave thanks, and said, Take this, and divide it among yourselves: For I say unto you, I will not drink of the fruit of the vine, until the kingdom of God shall come. And he took bread, and gave thanks, and brake it, and gave unto them, saying, This is my body which is given for you: this do in remembrance of me. Likewise also the cup after supper, saying, This cup is the new testament in my blood, which is shed for you.*

What should be a sobering and holy remembrance is turned into an abomination and a mockery by the heathen practice of a Catholic communion.

teachings.title: Receive the weak in faith, not to doubtful disputations
teachings.summary: Romans 14 teaches believers not to judge or argue with brethren over matters scripture leaves open, but to bear with weaker consciences and not put stumbling blocks before them.
teachings.text:
Romans chapter 14 is Paul giving particular application to these things regarding the consequences of our faith, turning it inwardly onto brothers in Christ; our role in edifying one another rather than debating and striving in doubtful disputations about things not clearly taught in scripture.

Something we see ourselves in any church or fellowship with other churches or individual Christians.

The Bible says we are to be a *whole body fitly joined together*, repeatedly stating we should be of one mind regarding the Gospel and the ministry of it. That if there are disputes between us, or trespasses against us, that we work it out within the congregation. Even unto church discipline. But in all things we are to strive together for the Gospel, and because of this, and loving one another, we shouldn't judge one another over things the Bible isn't firm on.

Understand that the Bible is the final authority on all matters of faith and practice. All scripture is given by God that we may be throughly furnished to all good works. Perfect. Complete. Especially with the catch-all, love each other as you love yourself. Putting others needs before your own. And the profit of others before yours. As much as possible live peaceably with all men.

And so, chapter 14 begins with a hypothetical situation to illustrate the point Paul is building to.

*Him that is weak in the faith receive ye, but not to doubtful disputations.*

This caveat  is important to understand what he is proposing; A person weak in the faith may hold themselves to a higher standard than the Bible calls for, that we being more stable in the faith may see as silly.

Right up front Paul is warning not to use the occasion to argue with them. Especially of they are so weak of faith, or babes, that either may dig in their heels at rebuke, and add to the Gospel their opinions. Doubtful disputations, arguments about unimportant things that ultimately rest on "if you disagree you aren't saved."

Get the picture here. We can assume these are both saved Christians who simply disagree on a matter of separation and sanctification that aren't spelled out, explicitly or implicitly in scripture. Paul uses eating of meat vs vegetarians, but He also applies it to celebration of holidays, even the first day of the week as sacred.

Other than the strong admonishment against eating meat sacrificed to idols in 1 Corinthians for example, even if you don't think the idol is anything but wood or molten metal, is clear. And the giving to us that all food is clean and good to eat, that is blessed in Christ by our thanksgiving, there is nothing that says we have to eat meat. Just as there's nothing against abstaining.

But one weak in the faith and consumed by guilt at eating an animal, or who sees holidays as unnecessary or even wrong in their conscience, we should be patient with. We shouldn't push them to do what's wrong in their mind, to stumble. Even if you think they're fools.

To love them, we shouldn't place stumbling blocks but rather edify them. Our job isn't to judge one another who believe and are not in open sin regarding clear teachings, over petty matters.

An example may be something like *The woman shall not wear that which pertaineth unto a man*, and applying it to all things, even specifically women's attire that has a shared element to what the male version is. Tee-shirts. Sweatshirts. Hoodies. Taking it beyond not crossdressing and wearing modest apparel as scripture teaches, but extending it to a higher level.

Just because they have a higher standard than the Bible calls for doesn't mean you should mock it or ridicule it, and by God if it is in your church and it is their standards and it isn't being placed as a work of righteousness, than not only remain quiet about it, but hold to it. Better to dress in the manner that is greater than the Bible calls for than to sow discord among the brethren and bring others to sin.

teachings.title: Mind not high things
teachings.summary: Believers must be of one mind and humble, not wise in their own conceits like Calvinists and trad Catholics, patiently guiding those less mature.
teachings.text:
*Be of the same mind one toward another. Mind not high things, but condescend to men of low estate. Be not wise in your own conceits.*

This admonition, to be of the same mind, is repeated in the epistles, that the churches which receive them understand that we all share one goal. Serve one Gospel. Look forward with certainty, the same hope.

It is why one of the 7 things God hates is a sower of discord among the brethren. It is why church discipline exists. But a church that is of one mind can do great things for the Lord.

But more so, see that the same caution to be of one mind, not at variance and strife, is coupled with the warning to Mind not high things, to not put ourselves as better than others, but rather condensed to the lowly. To not be wise in our own conceits.

Don't be a special boy.

If you have wisdom, if you have knowledge, it came from God and isn't yours. Be humble. If facing someone who isn't as far in their Christian walk as you, be patient and longsuffering and offer guidance, because that is why God gave you that knowledge. Don't be high-minded. Don't get caught up in theologies and intellectual pursuit, thinking you're better than the unlearned.

Special boys, your Calvinists, reform types, trad Caths, etc, full of vanity and the wisdom of the world, hold themselves up as better than others, full of hypocrisy.

But we shouldn't be. Rather knowing that we serve God and love others, seek their profit, not our own vainglory.

teachings.title: Present your bodies a living sacrifice
teachings.summary: Doctrine must be applied by presenting ourselves holy in service, not conformed to the world, each using his gifts to edify the one body.
teachings.text:
Having established all things, Paul now begins the practical application of the doctrines he has laid out. My favorite sermons are those that really tear into the meat of the word and then give practical application, how that doctrine can change your life and make you more able to work for God.

Knowledge and wisdom.

It isn't enough to know the word or have understanding of how it all connects, without taking the implications and applying it to our lives. How to be doers of the word and not hearers only.

Paul, in the letter to the Romans, lays out some heavy doctrine in dense language, the revelation of God, the reprobate doctrine, salvation by grace through faith alone, to the Greek and Jew alike, the understanding of God's grace and the purpose of our salvation. And the understanding of a spiritual Israel, not of the flesh.

But what then?

Chapter 12, in clear and concise language tells us.

That we present our bodies as a loving sacrifice, without blemish, which is our service, separated to the Gospel. Be holy that we may be better able to be of service to God. Vessels fitted for glory. Blameless.

This isn't an appeal to hit the gym and not eat poorly. Our bodies are corruptible, and flesh is going to lead us to sin. It is about walking in the spirit that we may not fulfil the lusts of that flesh, and by example bring others to Christ.

He writes, *be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind*, which comes from walking in the spirit. To know the will of God. Proving, testing to see what is acceptable.

We are to remain humble, understanding that to every man of faith God has shaped to a purpose. Not all have the same gifts, the same talents, but all are members of the same body, which is Christ. None more important or less important. A similar theme Found in **1 Corinthians 12**:

*But now are they many members, yet but one body. And the eye cannot say unto the hand, I have no need of thee: nor again the head to the feet, I have no need of you.*

And so each of us should seek to use the talents we have to edify the whole of the body of believers.

*Having then gifts differing according to the grace that is given to us, whether prophecy, let us prophesy according to the proportion of faith; Or ministry, let us wait on our ministering: or he that teacheth, on teaching; Or he that exhorteth, on exhortation: he that giveth, let him do it with simplicity; he that ruleth, with diligence; he that sheweth mercy, with cheerfulness.*

So, to our measure, we all make perfect the will of God. And we see too, that attitude is everything.

teachings.title: The passover lamb and the Lord's supper
teachings.summary: The Passover ordinance pictured Christ the Lamb, and at His last supper Jesus turned it into a new memorial ordinance, the Lord's supper, done in remembrance of Him.
teachings.text:
We find Jesus, now just one day from His crucifixion, very desirous to eat the passover. He mentions this desire repeatedly, telling His disciples to go and find such and such room, and prepare *where I shall eat the passover with my disciples.*

This is the first of the holy days of the year, which begins in spring in the Hebrew calendar, the first month *Adar*.
10 days in, the lamb without blemish is brought before the people, separated from the flock. On the 14th day the lamb is slain before the congregation. The blood spread with hyssop upon the wooden door posts, in remembrance of the first passover where this saved those within the home from the angel of death, given as an ordinance by God that in future generations when asked by those children, *What mean ye by this service?*  That they would explain the sacrifice, what it meant, and how God delivered the people with the blood of the lamb. That they cast out the leaven of their households, and broke and ate unleavened bread in remembrance of their flight from Egypt.

And ordinance is a memorial service, a ritual that is designed as a picture of something, to be kept as a reminder to future generations so they would understand.

*And this day shall be unto you for a memorial; and ye shall keep it a feast to the LORD throughout your generations; ye shall keep it a feast by an ordinance for ever.*

God essentially saying, "Do this in memory of Me."

Jesus, intent to have this passover supper, before His betrayal and death, brings the disciples together, and immediately turns from the traditional Passover ordinance, the ritual observance with unleavened bread, the unfermented juice of the vine and the lamb, and gives unto them a new ordinance; what we call the Lord's supper.

Jesus being the lamb to be delivered to the high priests to be slaughtered. His body broken as the unleavened bread is broken. The cup of the fruit of the vine poured out, and divided, as His blood. Blood put upon the doorways of our hearts that we be saved from death. That it passover us.

The passover observance being a picture of Christ's death. The feast of unleavened bread, the forgiveness of sin. Being brought out of Egypt and to the promised land, a picture of our deliverance to the Kingdom of God.

This, Jesus last meal before betrayal, and in it He provides a new ordinance to be done in His memory, that when future generations may ask, *What mean ye by this service?* We have a ready answer.

The cup is the new testament in Jesus' blood, which is shed for us. The bread, His body that was broken upon the cross. We do this in memory of Jesus.

teachings.title: Women who ministered with Christ
teachings.summary: Men and women are equal in Christ with distinct roles, women serving greatly in the ministry while subject to their own fathers and husbands, and godly women follow when men fill their biblical roles.
teachings.text:
Luke chapter 8 opens with a shout out to various women who ministered with Christ and the apostles, introducing us to Mary Magdalene, Joanna and Susanna, "and many others" who were an important part of Jesus mission.

Fundamentalists often are accused (and by implication, the word of God) of not respecting women, or somehow being anti-Women. And while that may be true in some instances, a mature Christian who studies the word understands that men and women have unique roles, and a hierarchy in the home and during the assembly, but that in Christ all are equal, and the part women play in the ministry is often more important than what the average man in a church does.

Most men may volunteer, soul win, maybe even lead studies and speak on men's nights, but they work and support their families. Their time isn't devoted to the ministry as their primary role. While women, ideally home, keeping the house and bringing up children, often are more involved in day to day labors in the Gospel.

They can preach the Gospel soul winning. They are responsible for giving lessons in scripture to their children. They organize feasts of charity, visit one another in affliction and mourning, help each other with things that edify the congregation.

Yes, Jesus is the head of the church, and a qualified pastor must be a male. Yes they must remain silent during services and submit to their husbands. It is the nature of our roles as children of God, and for the best interests of everyone, women included.

But women are not subject to every man. They aren't there to be servants or slaves to every swinging Harry who walks through the door. They are subject to their father or their husband, in church, to the pastor (just as the men are), but not subservient to every male that comes along.

This is a loving and healthy relationship between the male and female that God intends. Not "get me a sammich" despising of girls.

Here we see that two well connected women provided wealth from their status and station to enable Christ His ministry. They traveled with the disciples. On Pentecost, they were among those preaching the Gospel to the crowd, getting people saved. Paul's epistles are filled with praise for women who labored with him in evangelism and in the churches he helped plant.

Much is made of lamenting that women today are horrible. But the Bible teaches us they needn't be, and that it generally stems from men abandoning their roles, which in turn leads women to abandon theirs. (Looking at you [Barack](https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Judges%204&version=KJV)).

Men are to lead, by being faithful to Christ, obedient to God, loving unto death for the women in their care.

Men filling their biblical roles leads to women who do. And that in turn leads to a generation of godly children. And the glory of God increases. More souls are reached with the Gospel. Like Jesus earthly ministry and the early churches of the NT. We need to keep this in mind even more so today.

teachings.title: Full Assurance and Not Forsaking the Assembly
teachings.summary: Forgiven believers should not cling to guilt but draw near in full assurance and assemble together to provoke one another to love and good works.
teachings.text:
And so to those who live by faith, the burden of our sin borne on the cross by Jesus, quickened and sealed by the Spirit, made temples of God, adopted heirs, part of His priesthood, an holy people, we should have full confidence in the covenant and patience towards the day of redemption.

We shouldn't be miserable. We shouldn't cling to guilt for sins and inequities God has forgiven and remembers no more.

*If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.*

This is the liberty which is found in Christ.

And so, by implication Paul encourages us;

*Let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and our bodies washed with pure water. Let us hold fast the profession of our faith without wavering; (for he is faithful that promised;) And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works: Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching.*

If we truly believe all of these truths and have faith in our salvation, then let us as brethren encourage and edify each other, and do good works with a clean conscience. Not selfishly trying to appease an angry God, not in dead works and fruitless sacrifices of bulls and goats, but as servants to the Lord who saved us. Free from the bonds of the law. Free from death and Hell. Out of the same grace and mercy shown to us by our Father.

It should be noted here that Paul encourages us, in the Spirit, to gather with other believers in an assembly for the purpose of building our faith and provoking each other to love and good works. Exhortation in the faith, especially as we see that day of Christ's return approaching.

This is an appeal to go to church. Note, not for salvation, not just because it's sin not to, not because you can lose your salvation if you don't. But like all good works, to the benefit of others and a reflection of the love God has shown us in our salvation.

Do not forsake the assembly, because by it we become more complete, more perfect and able to serve God better. And it will build your faith and patience, your knowledge of the Lord, bring blessings for your works as it brings more opportunities to serve others.

teachings.title: Ephesus Left Its First Love
teachings.summary: The first love the Ephesian church left was winning souls, and a church that stops preaching the gospel to every creature will have its candlestick removed.
teachings.text:
*Unto the angel of the church of Ephesus write; These things saith he that holdeth the seven stars in his right hand, who walketh in the midst of the seven golden candlesticks;*

Jesus begins using a descriptor of Himself, from the description given by John from His vision in chapter 1. Jesus is holding the angels of the 7 churches in His hand. He is walking in this midst of their candlesticks. His message is to the Ephesians, the church founded 30 odd years before the writing of Revelation, by Paul and the other evangelists. That had fornication in their midst back in Ephesians 1. Jesus goes on to praise their good qualities;

*I know thy works, and thy labour, and thy patience, and how thou canst not bear them which are evil: and thou hast tried them which say they are apostles, and are not, and hast found them liars: And hast borne, and hast patience, and for my name's sake hast laboured, and hast not fainted.*

All good things.

*Nevertheless I have somewhat against thee, because thou hast left thy first love. Remember therefore from whence thou art fallen, and repent, and do the first works; or else I will come unto thee quickly, and will remove thy candlestick out of his place, except thou repent.*

The Ephesians have left their first love. This is generally accepted as the spreading of the Gospel. They are working and laboring and being persecuted in Christ's name, trying false prophets who crept in unawares and rejecting them. But the first love of any church is the winning of souls to Christ. The joy of our salvation when fresh leads to our telling everyone about the good news. Churches grow from giving the Gospel. But many successful churches plateau and settle in with who they have, and get wrapped up in feasts of charity, laboring in their own community of believers while neglecting this command of Christ to preach the word to every creature. Without that, Jesus says, He will remove their candlestick. The church will die.

*But this thou hast, that thou hatest the deeds of the Nicolaitanes, which I also hate.*

Another compliment, that the church at Ephesus hates the deeds of the Nicolaitanes. We have to discern from this limited information that they were a group either led by or claiming to be followers of someone named Nicolas. Many speculate that it refers to Nicolas the proselyte from Antioch, who was elevated to decon along with Stephen and Philip back in Acts.

The doctrines refered to here, according to early writings and histories is that Nicolas, a pagan convert to the faith of the Jews, then accepting Jesus as the promised Christ, had the doctrine of despising the flesh, hating the material world, that he could better focus on the spiritual. The idea is given he was a just believer, but those who came after him took his views and drifted heavily into gnosticism. We can't know directly from scripture, but this seems very likely. It's also possible that gnostics took the name as a way of gaining legitimacy in the early churches, that they may creep in unawares, with damnable heresy.

*He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches; To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the midst of the paradise of God.*

The first promise to those who overcome, who believe on the Lord Jesus Christ for salvation, is the gift of eternal life. The eating of the fruit of the tree of life, in the midst of the paradise of God. The location is going to come up later in Revelation, but the important thing is the knowledge that we who believe in He that has overcome will be given of it to eat.

Recall in Genesis 3 that God banishes Adam and Eve from the Garden to prevent their eating of this tree themselves, having already eaten of the tree of knowledge of good and evil. Having sinned.

teachings.title: Revelation Is About Christ, Not Geopolitics
teachings.summary: Like all scripture Revelation centres on Christ, explains its own mysteries so it is not too hard to read, and names churches plural, not a universal church.
teachings.text:
We see here in chapter one that, like the rest of scripture, the focus is on Christ Jesus and the spiritual things of God. When we read any of the Bible, we should keep this our focus. Comparing spiritual things with spiritual. It greatly helps with rightly dividing the word of God.

John writes that it comes "*from Jesus Christ, who is the faithful witness, and the first begotten of the dead, and the prince of the kings of the earth. Unto him that loved us, and washed us from our sins in his own blood, And hath made us kings and priests unto God and his Father; to him be glory and dominion for ever and ever. Amen. Behold, he cometh with clouds; and every eye shall see him, and they also which pierced him: and all kindreds of the earth shall wail because of him. Even so, Amen."*

This is what it's all about. It isn't about geopolitics. It's not about which earthly nation or events we want it to be. It's not a warning to those "left behind." It is written to be a blessing to the saved that we may know God's will in the last days, the honor and glory of Jesus and His triumph of the resurrection, His reign, wrath, judgement and victory. We are called simply witness to His glory, amen.

Lord Jesus, who we are repeatedly told is "*Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end,"* He *which is, and which was, and which is to come, the Almighty*.

John describes the vision of Jesus He has:  *the Son of man, clothed with a garment down to the foot, and girt about the paps with a golden girdle.*
*His head and his hairs were white like wool, as white as snow; and his eyes were as a flame of fire; And his feet like unto fine brass, as if they burned in a furnace; and his voice as the sound of many waters.*
*And he had in his right hand seven stars: and out of his mouth went a sharp twoedged sword: and his countenance was as the sun shineth in his strength.*

He is radiant, fitted with a golden girdle, hair white, feet bronzed, and from His mouth comes the Word, a two-edged sword.

**Hebrews 4:12**
*For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.*

Some heretical blacks use this passage to claim Jesus is black. It's foolishness. His feet are like brass as if they'd been burned in a furnace, not natural pigmentation. Again, it is applying natural man things to what is spiritual that leads people to nonsense doctrine.

John says as he turned to witness Christ he sees seven stars and seven golden candlesticks. This is one of the many symbolic illustrations we will see as we go through Revelation. And these are the kinds of things that false prophets seize upon to claim that the book is too mysterious to understand directly. That one needs some gnostic process to understand. Yet, as we read on we see that each mystery is explained. Jesus says to John regarding the 7 stars/golden candlesticks;

*The mystery of the seven stars which thou sawest in my right hand, and the seven golden candlesticks. The seven stars are the angels of the seven churches: and the seven candlesticks which thou sawest are the seven churches.*

We aren't left to wonder about much. There are some hard passages and dark sayings contained in Revelation, but more often than not, they are explained in the narrative. God is not the author of confusion. Trust in the Spirit. So much of this is incredibly straightforward, it is a shame Satan has made people afraid to read Revelation. That confusion the devil has sown in the world keeps Christians from the blessing that is found in it.

So, now heading into chapter 2, recall that the 7 stars are the angels of the 7 churches, and the 7 candlesticks are the churches themselves.

Note, churches, plural. The idea of a single universal church is not biblical. They were independent and Christ led, New Testament churches from the beginning.

teachings.title: All scripture given by inspiration of God
teachings.summary: 2 Timothy 3 teaches that all scripture is inspired, preserved and sufficient for doctrine, so independent fundamental Baptist churches drawing doctrine from scripture alone are the only way.
teachings.text:
Paul, again in his final days, knowing he won't see Asia Minor and the churches he planted there or the evangelists like Timothy he's laid hands on and sent out, again, and having several of them turn from him in fear of persecution and shame of Paul's bonds, and several false teachers creep in to the churches to lead men shipwreck, is laying out the foundational doctrines for Timothy to remember and pass on. There's an urgency that allows Paul, in the Spirit to be as concise and precise as possible. It makes second Timothy one of the densest and deep books, despite it's brevity.

Here we see, in order, the Reprobate Doctrine, the names of Pharoah's court wizards (Jannes and Jambres), how reprobates will grow worse and worse over time, infiltrating houses, leading people astray, especially women. That God will give them what they deserve in the end.

We learn the sound doctrines taught of Paul, purpose, faith, longsuffering, charity, patience, and the assurance that ALL who live Godly in Christ will see persecution. Tribulations and trouble for His name's sake.

That faith comes from hearing and hearing by the Word of God. That scriptures make us wise unto salvation by faith in Jesus Christ. Faith alone, in Christ alone. Further, that *All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: That the man of God may be perfect, thoroughly furnished unto all good works.*

We get out doctrine from scripture. No other source, but the word of God. It is perfect, meaning complete. It is inspired. It is preserved. If it weren't preserved, how could it thoroughly furnish a man of God unto salvation through faith? Unto good works?

These doctrines are either denied or added to by denominations today. They deny reprobation. They deny salvation by faith alone. They deny scripture is preserved, inspired or even necessary for doctrine.

Even prot denominations that claim Sola Fide and Sola Scripta will add works to salvation and writings of "reformers" and church fathers to their faithless theology.

Biblical Fundamentalism is the only way. New Testament churches, independent, pastor led, engaged in preaching the Gospel to every creature, a believer's baptism, a congregation of believers studying the scriptures to be approved by God, charitable to the brethren, judge to the fatherless, honoring elders and widows indeed. Eating communal suppers, in Jesus name. Tithing that those who work to the edification of the assembly are given their due.

Awaiting the return of Jesus to save us out of great tribulation, and bring the wrath of God upon the wicked and profane. The rapture and resurrection of the saints. The millennial reign. The marriage feast of the lamb. Giving glory to God forever and ever. Amen.

Everything else is doctrines of devils, having the appearance of righteousness, a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof. From these, the Bible says, flee.

teachings.title: Forgive and comfort the repentant
teachings.summary: As Paul told the church to forgive and restore the disciplined brother, parents should discipline in love and then truly forgive and forget, or they teach their children a works-based relationship with God.
teachings.text:
Chapter 2 continues Paul's introduction, speaking now as to why he hadn't come to them, *with a rod,* as promised in his first epistle to them, saying he decided in part to not come to them "in heaviness" to grieve them.

As we saw in 1 Corinthians, Paul had laid into them pretty hard, especially in chapter 5 regarding one member and his wicked fornication.

Paul says to them that he considers them his sons in Christ, having asked them to follow him as a father who brought them to the gospel, and like a father, scourging those he loves, Paul says his chastisement was necessary but he doesn't want them to mistake it for anything other than his love of them.

He says in verse 5 that it wasn't personal. He's not doing this out of hurt feelings.

And likewise, as he's showing kindness to those he'd chastised, he says to them that they should be forgiving to those in the church that they punished as he'd called for, and they having repented, be welcomed back and comforted that they not fall back into sin.

We are never to tolerate or enable other Christians sins, especially those that lead to church discipline, but when a Christian makes a sincere turn around, we are to be gracious like God is with us, daily. Forgiveness of trespasses.

Paul says if they've forgiven some their sin and brought them back from being backslidden, it's good enough for him, because it is good enough for Christ.

This may be specifically the man who was sleeping with his step-mother, but it reads as a more general item. We should be happy to forgive and forget, just as eagerly as we are to condemn and rebuke.

As a parent treats their child, which is how Paul looks at those he's won to Christ, this is an incredibly important concept to master. How we love our children, including how we discipline and forgive, is an imprint in their minds of how God works, and by showing firm hand, but loving kindness and forgiveness, the same as He shows us, we are demonstrating to them His love and grace.

When we are resentful, angry, taking it personally and overcharging them, failing to forgive and forget, they may *be swallowed up with much sorrow.* It is how Satan gains an advantage in their lives.

Many parents create a barter system in place of love, where everything is transactional. They may forgive but not forget, throwing past behavior at their child, holding it against them. Many parents don't even realize they are doing it. This behavior builds within a child the seeds for a works-based relationship with God, and can cause all sorts of problems in their lives. Never being "good enough." Never having healthy relationships with others. Never really understanding the charitable love and grace we have in hope through Christ Jesus. Maybe even bringing them to reprobation in the end, bitter against you and so bitter against God.

teachings.title: Remove thy candlestick is not losing salvation
teachings.summary: Revelation 1:20 says the candlesticks are the churches, so Christ's warning to remove a candlestick means a church's standing and fellowship, not a saint's salvation.
teachings.text:
Someone in the ApeMountain chat was asking about the verses in Revelation 2 and 3 where Jesus tells John about His issues with the 7 various independent churches. The question was basically aren't those verses where Jesus tells the churches to repent or He will "remove thy candlestick" saying they are going to lose their salvation?

The answer is a resounding no. As the Bible makes clear in **Revelation 1:12-20**, the candlesticks represent the churches themselves and their fellowship and blessing with Jesus:

*12 And I turned to see the voice that spake with me. And being turned, I saw seven golden candlesticks;*

*13 And in the midst of the seven candlesticks one like unto the Son of man, clothed with a garment down to the foot, and girt about the paps with a golden girdle.*

*14 His head and his hairs were white like wool, as white as snow; and his eyes were as a flame of fire;*

*15 And his feet like unto fine brass, as if they burned in a furnace; and his voice as the sound of many waters.*

*16 And he had in his right hand seven stars: and out of his mouth went a sharp twoedged sword: and his countenance was as the sun shineth in his strength.*

*17 And when I saw him, I fell at his feet as dead. And he laid his right hand upon me, saying unto me, Fear not; I am the first and the last:*

*18 I am he that liveth, and was dead; and, behold, I am alive for evermore, Amen; and have the keys of hell and of death.*

*19 Write the things which thou hast seen, and the things which are, and the things which shall be hereafter;*

*20 The mystery of the seven stars which thou sawest in my right hand, and the seven golden candlesticks. The seven stars are the angels of the seven churches: and the seven candlesticks which thou sawest are the seven churches.*

There's a myth that the dark sayings in Revelation are mysterious, but frequently when John seems confused or unsure Jesus or an angel will say "here's what this means." Obviously some remains through a glass darkly, but much of it is explained.

When Christ says "*Repent, and do the first works; or else I will come unto thee quickly, and will remove thy candlestick,"* He is literally speaking of their authority, hedge of protection, etc, as His church in fellowship with Him. He doesn't threaten those saints with damnation, because that would contradict the Gospel given that led them to being God's servants.

Jesus repeatedly says something like "He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches" in His letters to these churches. Far too many do not have an ear to hear.

teachings.title: Jude: trees without fruit, twice dead
teachings.summary: Jude warns saved believers to keep reprobate, ungodly men out of the churches while still winning souls with compassion and with fear.
teachings.text:
We see in Jude an epistle to saved Christians, to whom the Gospel had already been delivered, warning them of those others who are reprobate in the faith, trees without fruit, twice-dead, plucked up...

There's reason this parallel book to 2 Peter, reiterating many of the same themes and warnings, and echoing Romans 1, is included right before Revelation.

It is both a warning to keep these abominations out of the various local churches and to win souls to Christ, saving who they can with charity and if need be, fear, warning them of the fire that awaits those unrighteous and ungodly men who tempt the unsaved away from the true Gospel.
